title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Veterinary Medicine (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Veterinary Medicine (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not correct about function of lairage in abattoirs
options: It helps to perform proper ante mortem examination
It is a place where animals rest before slaughter
It helps to improve the meat quality
It increases the exposure of animals for stressful condition
questions.explanation: Lairage is designed to reduce stress in animals before slaughter, not increase it. The other options are correct functions of lairage.

questions.questionText: Cytological examination of semen is a helpful diagnostic option for
questions.explanation: Cytological examination of semen can reveal inflammatory cells and pathogens indicative of orchitis/epididymitis.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not effect of transport on food animal during transportation
questions.explanation: Transport typically causes weight loss due to stress, not gain. The other options are common transport effects.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a common name for lactose fermenter Enterobacteriaceae?
questions.explanation: Coliform is the collective term for lactose-fermenting Enterobacteriaceae like E. coli, Klebsiella, etc.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a key component of a successful national control program for dog-mediated rabies
options: Effective control of the dog population
questions.explanation: 'None' is incorrect as all listed components are essential for rabies control.

questions.questionText: When the effect of combination of two effective drugs is greater than individual effect, we say the drugs have
questions.explanation: Synergistic effect occurs when combined drug effect exceeds their individual effects.

questions.questionText: What describes the action of a drug on the body of animals receiving it?
questions.explanation: Pharmacodynamics specifically studies how drugs affect the body (mechanism of action, therapeutic effects, side effects). Pharmacokinetics is how the body processes drugs, psology is dosage science, and toxicology studies poisons.

questions.questionText: A veterinarian can assess the appetite of the animal by observing the following reactions to
options: Number of days that the animal is under treatment with vitamin B complex
Offering of feed or by the amount of feed available that has not been eaten
Checking the health status of the animal
questions.explanation: Direct observation of feeding behavior/uneaten feed is most reliable for appetite assessment.

questions.questionText: A veterinarian on duty has suspected GI nematode infection in sheep and ordered laboratory examination to confirm the case. Which one of the following pairs of techniques is suitable for immediate diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Direct smear (quick) + flotation (sensitive) provide rapid nematode egg detection.

questions.questionText: Which one is not correct about proper transportation of food animals to slaughterhouse?
options: Ensure animal welfare and meat safety
Improve the quality of the meat
Predispose the animals to stressful conditions
Minimize losses of the animal or carcass
questions.explanation: Proper transport should minimize stress, not predispose animals to it.

questions.questionText: One of the following supplements of culture media favours the growth of Mycobacterium bovis?
questions.explanation: Mycobactin is an iron-chelating growth factor required by M. bovis.

questions.questionText: For which of the following disease is that Cattle are the dead end host?
questions.explanation: Cattle are dead-end hosts for MCF (sheep are reservoir).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example for Gram negative cocci?
questions.explanation: Neisseria is Gram-negative cocci; others are Gram-positive or rods.

questions.questionText: What do we call the entry of drugs into the blood plasma?
questions.explanation: Absorption is the process of drug entry into systemic circulation.

questions.questionText: Which one is the correct reason why a dog that has bitten a person should be quarantined for 10-14 days?
options: To provide medical care for the dog
If the dog dies within 2-10 days, to recommend starting of post exposure vaccination or continuation if already started
To recommend post exposure vaccination of the person bitten by the dog if the dog has not shown any clinical sign
To consider the dog free of rabies, if it does not show any furious clinical sign
questions.explanation: 10-14 day quarantine observes for rabies signs; death would indicate rabies risk.

questions.questionText: Auscultation, percussion and palpation are all together the major methods used for examination of which organs?
questions.explanation: These techniques are primary for lung examination (respiratory sounds, resonance, fremitus).

questions.questionText: Which of the following does not describe Marek's disease
options: It is caused by Gallid Herpesvirus 1 virus
It causes thickening of peripheral nerves
It results paralysis of leg and wing of infected chicken
It is a lymphnomatous and neuropathic disease of poultry
questions.explanation: Marek's is caused by Gallid herpesvirus 2 (not 1).

questions.questionText: Which of the following surgical activity is non-elective?
options: Removal of large and pedanculated papilloma from the flank
questions.explanation: C-sections are emergency procedures; others are elective.

questions.questionText: In Assosa Veterinary Clinic, a cow was treated against trypanosomosis by genuine diminazene diaceturate. Seven and ten days after treatment, blood samples from the same animal became positive for the parasite. How do you explain the reason why the animal was still positive?
options: Diminazene was not the correct treatment
questions.explanation: Rapid recurrence of parasitemia after treatment with genuine diminazene suggests drug resistance, especially given the short timeframe (7-10 days) which is too quick for reinfection. Drug resistance in trypanosomes is a growing concern in many regions.

questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect statement about the cross-sectional study
options: Completed faster and more economical than other studies
Not appropriate for diseases of short duration
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional studies are prone to certain biases (selection, recall).

questions.questionText: The most commonly used site of caesarian operation to assist parturition in cattle is
options: The left lower flank in an oblique incision
The right lower flank in an oblique incision
The left upper flank in an oblique incision
The right upper flank in an oblique incision
questions.explanation: Left flank approach avoids rumen and provides best access to uterus.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not correct
options: Fetal Maceration results from death of the fetus followed by dilation of the cervix and incomplete abortion or dystocia
biochemical change to sperm that allows the true acrosome reaction to occur is referred as capacitation
Uterine prolapse occurs shortly after parturition and it is not a true emergency as hypocalcemia
Treatment of pyometra may involve the use of prostaglandin and myotonic drugs
questions.explanation: Uterine prolapse IS a true emergency requiring immediate intervention.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false statement?
options: Resazurin reduction and methylene blue reduction tests use similar principles except time difference
Organoleptic tests use sense organs to check any abnormalities
Alcohol test is more sensitive than clot on boiling test to check spoilage of milk
Production of lactic acid by Lactobacillus species has little effect on the quality of milk
questions.explanation: Lactic acid production significantly affects milk quality (pH, taste, coagulation).

questions.questionText: If administration of a medication produces a desired result, it is said to have
questions.explanation: Therapeutic effect refers to desired pharmacological outcome.

questions.questionText: Among the surgical manipulations of cattle, which one is approached in upper left flank?
questions.explanation: Rumenotomy is performed via left paralumbar fossa (upper left flank).

questions.questionText: Which technique can be used for determination of parasite burden?
questions.explanation: McMaster chamber quantifies eggs per gram of feces (EPG).

questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect statement about vital parameters
options: Athletic animals have a less frequent pulse than non-athletic animals of the same species
Age and body size of animals are directly related with vital parameters
Physiological status of animals can not affect the normal vital parameters
Exercise increases the vital parameters of animals
questions.explanation: Pregnancy, lactation, etc. DO affect vital parameters.

questions.questionText: The most effective antigens are
options: Have a molecular mass less than 10KD
questions.explanation: The most effective antigens are: 1) Foreign to the host (immunogenicity), 2) Complex in structure (multiple epitopes), 3) Large (>10kD for T-cell recognition), and 4) Particulate/insoluble (better processing). The other options describe poor antigens.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not part of external hernia
options: hernial ring which is the opening in the abdominal wall
hernial sac formed by the parietal peritoneum and the covering skin
questions.explanation: Urine is not a component of hernia anatomy.

questions.questionText: ____ is a condition in which eyelashes are abnormally positioned and grow inward
questions.explanation: Trichiasis is inward-growing lashes; distichiasis is extra lash row.

questions.questionText: As cells of the erythrocytic series get matured, one of the following does not happen
options: Their cytoplasm changes from bluish to reddish
The nucleus turns pyknotic and disappears in mammals
Their cytoplasm changes from reddish to bluish
questions.explanation: Erythroid maturation: blue (ribosomes) → pink (hemoglobin).

questions.questionText: Choke is characterized by:-
questions.explanation: Choke specifically refers to esophageal obstruction.

questions.questionText: A single antigenic determinant is called
questions.explanation: Epitope is the specific antigen portion binding to antibody.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the best design to study the incidence of a disease?
questions.explanation: Cohort studies measure incidence by following groups over time.

questions.questionText: Which of the following technique can be used to help and prevent a suture from slipping off the tissues such as uterine stump?
questions.explanation: Transfixation sutures penetrate tissue mass to prevent slippage.

questions.questionText: A community perception was assessed in a random sample of its residents by telephone questionnaire. Vector borne disease outbreaks are strongly associated with season. This study design is best described as which one of the following
questions.explanation: Single-timepoint survey = cross-sectional design.

questions.questionText: One of the following statement is true about oxidase test
options: It used to indicate the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen and water
It indicates the presence of cytochrome oxidase in the bacterial cell.
Brucella melitensis is oxidase test negative bacteria
None of the above is true
questions.explanation: The oxidase test detects cytochrome c oxidase enzyme in bacteria. This is different from catalase test (which detects H2O2 breakdown). Brucella melitensis is actually oxidase positive, not negative.

questions.questionText: Which domestic breed protruding tongue during grazing?
questions.explanation: Cattle protrude tongue to grasp forage; sheep use lips.

questions.questionText: Long term stress such as during transportation results in poor meat quality such as
questions.explanation: Chronic stress depletes glycogen → high pH → dark firm dry (DFD) meat.

questions.questionText: One of the following does not characterize the use of local anesthesia
options: Increases blood perfusion in peripheral organs
questions.explanation: Local anesthetics cause vasoconstriction, reducing perfusion.

questions.questionText: The owner of a three-days-old calf has complained that his animal is exhibiting signs of weakness, anorexia, and a bloody scour. On physical examination, the calf was found febrile. On farm visit, the calf pen was found to be very wet and dirty. Therefore based on these findings which one is more appropriate tentative diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Bloody diarrhea + fever + poor hygiene suggests Salmonella.

questions.questionText: Action-research can be understood as
options: kind of research being carried out to solve a specific problem
questions.explanation: Action-research focuses on solving practical problems through iterative cycles.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is drumstick-shaped sporulating organism?
questions.explanation: C. tetani has characteristic drumstick spores (terminal bulges).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not part of clinical examination?
questions.explanation: Equipment check is preparatory, not part of the actual examination.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following description is not associated with the animal freedom?
options: Freedom to express its normal behaviour
Freedom not be used by human
questions.explanation: Animal welfare accepts humane use; absolute non-use isn't a principle.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false?
options: Fever or pyrexia is the state where hyperthermia is combined with toxemia, as in most infectious diseases
Hyperthermia is simple elevation of the temperature past the critical point, as in heat stroke
Tachycardia, or decreased pulse rate, is common and occurs in most cases of septicemia
Hypothermia, a subnormal body temperature, occurs in shock
questions.explanation: The statement is false because tachycardia is INCREASED heart rate (not decreased). In septicemia, tachycardia is common due to inflammatory mediators and compensatory mechanisms. Bradycardia is decreased heart rate.

questions.questionText: Which specious of animals is a classic example of followers?
questions.explanation: Sheep exhibit strong following behavior in flocks.

questions.questionText: Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is the attenuated form of which specie of Mycobacterium?
questions.explanation: BCG derived from attenuated M. bovis strain.

questions.questionText: Which research type is useful to understand social values and practices in veterinary science?
questions.explanation: Qualitative methods explore social/cultural dimensions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a method of restraining cattle?
questions.explanation: Nose twitches are for horses; not used in cattle restraint.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is incorrect about Taenia saginata
options: The final host is human being
questions.explanation: T. saginata forms cysticercus (C. bovis), not coenurus.

questions.questionText: The main aim of fasting before slaughtering is:-
options: To minimize contamination of the carcasses
To minimize the effluent from abattoir
To reduce weight of the gastrointestinal content
questions.explanation: Fasting empties GI tract to reduce fecal contamination during evisceration.

questions.questionText: Which one is not considered as pre-slaughter care to ensure meat quality and safety?
questions.explanation: Pre-slaughter fasting (no feed) is standard practice.

questions.questionText: For which one of the following conditions, anesthesia is not used?
options: If patients are allergic to anesthesia
questions.explanation: Allergy contraindicates anesthetic use (risk of anaphylaxis).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the approach for Gastrotomy in dog?
questions.explanation: Flank approach is for ruminants; dogs use ventral midline.

questions.questionText: Platelets develop from:-
questions.explanation: Platelets are cytoplasmic fragments of megakaryocytes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of prospective cohort studies?
options: Ideal study design for rare diseases that take a long time to develop
Relatively cheap and quick to conduct
questions.explanation: Prospective cohorts establish cause-effect sequence clearly.

questions.questionText: Select the parasite that always occurs extracellular
questions.explanation: Trypanosomes circulate in blood; others are intracellular.

questions.questionText: One of the following is wrong in dealing with dogs as a veterinarian
options: Never compromise the welfare of the animals during restraining
Never catch a stray dog showing abnormal behavior under any condition
Never touch dog feces with bare hand
questions.explanation: Abnormal dogs MUST be caught (safely) for rabies evaluation.

questions.questionText: All of the following statements are true regarding particular veterinary surgical procedures, except
options: It should be mentally visualized prior to commencing the operation
Presence of suture, surgical instrument and experience of the surgeon should be considered
Cost benefit analysis should be analyzed before conducting the procedure
Animals necessarily be fasted from feed and water before operation
questions.explanation: Some emergency surgeries proceed without fasting.

questions.questionText: Rafoxanide is a drug of choice for treating against which parasite?
questions.explanation: Rafoxanide is a salicylanilide effective against liver flukes.

questions.questionText: What describes the action of the body on a drug administered to an animal?
questions.explanation: Pharmacokinetics: ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion).

questions.questionText: What is the main factor that should be considered during selecting of research problem?
questions.explanation: Relevance to field needs is primary in problem selection.

questions.questionText: Oxytocin treatment is indicated in cow
options: To hasten uterine involution following dystocia
questions.explanation: Oxytocin promotes uterine contractions for involution.

questions.questionText: Among the following, identify the most harmful species of equines Strongylus parasite
questions.explanation: S. vulgaris causes verminous arteritis (life-threatening).

questions.questionText: Cryptorchidism is a failure of one or both testicles to descend into the scrotum. It is the most common disorder of sexual development in
questions.explanation: Cryptorchidism prevalence highest in dogs (especially purebreds).

questions.questionText: An ideal anthelminthic is characterized by the following, except:-
options: Stay in the host tissue for long time
questions.explanation: Prolonged tissue persistence increases toxicity risk.

questions.questionText: One of the following chemical is used to differentiate the egg of Fasciola from that of Paraphistomum under the microscope
questions.explanation: K2Cr2O7 preserves Fasciola eggs (yellow-brown) vs Paramphistomum.

questions.questionText: Select the wrongly matched pairs
options: Prognosis-clinical signs exhibited by animal under investigation
Diagnosis-Establishing the nature and cause of disease
Differential diagnosis-Helps determine which one of several diseases is producing the signs
questions.explanation: Prognosis predicts outcome, not current signs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of prospective cohort studies?
options: Ideal study design for rare diseases that take a long time to develop
Relatively cheap and quick to conduct
questions.explanation: Prospective cohort studies excel at establishing temporal sequences (cause-effect relationships) by following subjects forward in time. Attrition is actually a disadvantage, they're expensive and time-consuming, and case-control studies (not cohort) are better for rare diseases.

questions.questionText: Select the parasite that always occurs extracellular
questions.explanation: Trypanosoma species are extracellular parasites that live in the blood and tissue fluids of their hosts, unlike Plasmodium, Theileria, and Babesia which are intracellular parasites.

questions.questionText: One of the following is wrong in dealing with dogs as a veterinarian
options: Never compromise the welfare of the animals during restraining
Never catch a stray dog showing abnormal behavior under any condition
Never touch dog feces with bare hand
questions.explanation: While caution is needed, veterinarians must sometimes handle stray dogs showing abnormal behavior (like potential rabies cases) using proper protective measures. Complete avoidance isn't practical for veterinary professionals.

questions.questionText: All of the following statements are true regarding particular veterinary surgical procedures, except
options: It should be mentally visualized prior to commencing the operation
Presence of suture, surgical instrument and experience of the surgeon should be considered
Cost benefit analysis should be analyzed before conducting the procedure
Animals necessarily be fasted from feed and water before operation
questions.explanation: While fasting is common, it's not always necessary (e.g., in emergency surgeries). The other options are essential considerations for veterinary surgical procedures.

questions.questionText: Rafoxanide is a drug of choice for treating against which parasite?
questions.explanation: Rafoxanide is a salicylanilide compound effective against liver flukes (Fasciola hepatica) and some gastrointestinal parasites, but primarily used for fascioliasis.

questions.questionText: What describes the action of the body on a drug administered to an animal?
questions.explanation: Pharmacokinetics describes how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and excretes drugs (ADME processes), while pharmacodynamics describes drug effects on the body.

questions.questionText: What is the main factor that should be considered during selecting of research problem?
questions.explanation: While all factors matter, relevance (scientific/ practical importance) is paramount in research problem selection to ensure meaningful contribution to knowledge or practice.

questions.questionText: Oxytocin treatment is indicated in cow
options: To hasten uterine involution following dystocia
questions.explanation: Oxytocin stimulates uterine contractions, aiding involution after difficult birth. It doesn't synchronize estrus or induce ovulation, and isn't primary treatment for endometritis.

questions.questionText: Among the following, identify the most harmful species of equines Strongylus parasite
questions.explanation: Strongylus vulgaris is most pathogenic due to its larval migration through mesenteric arteries, causing verminous arteritis and thromboembolic colic.

questions.questionText: Cryptorchidism is a failure of one or both testicles to descend into the scrotum. It is the most common disorder of sexual development in
questions.explanation: Cryptorchidism occurs most frequently in dogs (especially certain breeds), with reported incidence of 1-15% compared to <1% in stallions and lower in other species.

questions.questionText: An ideal anthelminthic is characterized by the following, except:-
options: Stay in the host tissue for long time
questions.explanation: While prolonged activity can be beneficial, ideal anthelmintics should have selective toxicity (not persist too long in host tissues) to minimize residue issues.

questions.questionText: One of the following chemical is used to differentiate the egg of Fasciola from that of Paraphistomum under the microscope
questions.explanation: Potassium dichromate preserves Fasciola eggs (yellow-brown, operculated) while Paraphistomum eggs (colorless, smaller) are better differentiated using this method.

questions.questionText: Select the wrongly matched pairs
options: Prognosis-clinical signs exhibited by animal under investigation
Diagnosis-Establishing the nature and cause of disease
Differential diagnosis-Helps determine which one of several diseases is producing the signs
questions.explanation: Prognosis refers to predicted disease outcome, not clinical signs. Clinical signs are part of diagnosis. Other pairs are correctly matched.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about Rabies?
options: Immediate and through washing of wounds with soap and water after bitten by rabid animal is an important prevention way
Post-exposure vaccination is unlikely to be of value in animals
Euthanasia of suspect animals must be avoided
questions.explanation: Immediate wound washing with soap and water is crucial as it can reduce viral load by up to 90%. Post-exposure prophylaxis CAN be effective in animals if given very early, and euthanasia is often necessary for rabies-suspect animals to prevent spread and for testing.

questions.questionText: Best antidote for organophosphate poisoning?
questions.explanation: Atropine is primary antidote for organophosphate toxicity as it blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors. Pralidoxime may also be used for nicotinic effects.

questions.questionText: Tuberculosis is transmitted by
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium bovis can spread via aerosol (main route), placenta, milk, and contaminated semen during AI, making all options correct transmission routes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following stage of Fasciola infects its snail intermediate hosts?
questions.explanation: Miracidia hatch from eggs and actively penetrate snails. Rediae and cercariae develop within snails, while metacercariae infect final hosts on vegetation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following diagnostic tool is prescribed test for detection of PPR for international trade?
questions.explanation: Competitive ELISA is OIE's prescribed test for PPR in international trade because: 1) High specificity and sensitivity, 2) Can differentiate vaccinated from infected animals (DIVA), 3) Suitable for mass screening, and 4) More standardized than virus neutralization.

questions.questionText: One of the following clinical material is preferred for isolation and identification of FMD Virus except
questions.explanation: FMDV is best isolated from vesicular fluid/epithelium during acute phase. Blood (leukocyte fraction) can be used early, but urine is not a standard sample.

questions.questionText: Which one is true on Pastoral Extension?
options: Paid no attention to the emergence of agro-pastoralism
Consider maintenance and sustainability of Infrastructure
questions.explanation: Effective pastoral extension programs focus on infrastructure sustainability (water points, grazing management) alongside other development aspects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is true regarding veterinary surgery?
options: Non elective surgery is performed on emergency basis so allows necessarily preoperative assessment of the patient.
Elective surgery is performed on emergency basis so that allows necessarily preoperative assessment of patient.
Elective surgery is performed on non-emergency basis so allows preoperative Assessment of patient.
Non elective surgery is performed on emergency basis and may do not allow Preoperative assessment of the patient.
questions.explanation: Non-elective (emergency) surgeries often limit preoperative assessment due to urgency, while elective procedures allow thorough evaluation.

questions.questionText: Name a substance which, when combined with antigen, non-specifically enhances the resulting immune response to that antigen.
questions.explanation: Adjuvants (e.g., aluminum salts, oil emulsions) boost immune responses to co-administered antigens without specific antigenic properties themselves.

questions.questionText: A poisoning chemical used as a chemical to control stray dogs in Ethiopia is
questions.explanation: Strychnine, though highly toxic and inhumane, has been historically used for stray dog control in some regions including parts of Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: One of the following does not contribute to errors in bone marrow sampling from live animal
options: Experience of the person taking the sample
Difficulty in obtaining sufficient volume of sample
questions.explanation: Operator skill affects success but isn't an 'error'. Blood contamination, inadequate samples, and quantification challenges are common technical errors.

questions.questionText: Which Newcastle disease virus strain causes mild infections of the respiratory tract?
questions.explanation: Lentogenic strains (e.g., LaSota) cause mild respiratory signs. Mesogenic are moderately virulent, velogenic cause severe systemic disease.

questions.questionText: A congenital defect which pose persistent opening between the Aorta and Pulmonary artery is
questions.explanation: PDA is failure of fetal ductus arteriosus to close, creating abnormal aorto-pulmonary connection. Others involve different cardiac structures.

questions.questionText: In veterinary clinical diagnosis, which of the following is not a relevant data during history taking?
options: The family size of the owner
questions.explanation: Owner's family size is irrelevant to patient assessment. Animal identifiers (color, species), and demographic data (age, sex) are essential history components.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement best describes one health approach?
options: It requires a multidisciplinary and multisectoral coordination for its success
It is under human health discipline
It is under veterinary public health discipline
Environmental health has insignificant role in one health approach
questions.explanation: One Health emphasizes collaborative, cross-sectoral approaches linking human, animal, and environmental health for optimal outcomes.

questions.questionText: One of the following is common characteristics of Fasciola and Schistosoma.
questions.explanation:
Both Fasciola (liver fluke) and Schistosoma (blood fluke) require snail intermediate hosts in their life cycles.
Fasciola is hermaphroditic while Schistosoma has separate sexes (option a incorrect).
Only Fasciola's infective stage is metacercaria (option b incorrect).
While Fasciola affects the liver, Schistosoma primarily affects blood vessels (option d partially incorrect).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a cause of environmental mastitis?
questions.explanation:
Staphylococcus aureus is primarily a contagious mastitis pathogen transmitted during milking.
The other three (Klebsiella, E. coli, S. uberis) are environmental pathogens acquired between milkings from the cow's environment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a common cause of constipation?
options: Diseases of the fore-stomach and abomasum causing failure of outflow
questions.explanation:
Partial obstruction of the small intestine typically causes diarrhea (not constipation) due to increased fluid secretion.
The other options are well-established causes of constipation in animals.
